targets: every new string in both trees

entries.detail: User-facing copy uses passive voice "cannot be recalled" (to be + past participle). This appears in a confirmation dialog shown to users. Active voice should name the actor (e.g., "We cannot recall notifications once sent" or "You cannot undo notifications already sent").

Ran `rg -n '"[^"]{3,}"'` and `rg -n '
'` over interstice/web/panel.html and README.md, plus targeted rg for ' (has|have|is|was|sent|added|matched|found)' over the akin Social flow .swift files and the three FrontBackModels files (AuthorVisibility.swift, FollowNotifications.swift, MatchmakingProfile.swift), then read the matched lines in context. The Social/FrontBackModels strings ("A questionnaire you follow has a new question.", "People answering will see that you wrote this question.", "You are not following anything yet", etc.) all put the reader or a person in subject position with complete objects; no offenses there. panel.html line 582: `
Amazon could not open this book
` names a brand (Amazon) as the grammatical subject narrating a failure, in a sentence that exists to tell the reader about their own situation (their book did not load) and could be rewritten with the reader as subject. It does not qualify for the status-line exception since it claims a direct consequence for the reader (the book they were reading is now unavailable). Replacement: "Your book didn't open" (with the existing #reader-failed-why detail div still carrying the Amazon-specific explanation, and the adjacent "Try again" button still giving the reader something to do). A second nearby candidate, panel.html:1406 `
Amazon is asking you to sign in
`, keeps Amazon as subject but already contains "you" as the addressed party and gives the reader a clear next action via the following button, so I did not flag it as a second offense; it is a softer case than the one flagged. No such pattern was found in interstice/README.md.
entries.rule_title: Copy narrates the system instead of addressing the reader

entries.detail: Enumerated visible labels/badges/buttons/toggles across the targets and wrote a one-sentence purpose for each using only on-screen context; none needed a second screen or a tap to understand, and I found no analog of the "(Not this time)" trigger. Checked: akin/akin/Flows/Social/ProfileSwitcherView.swift (lines 25-91: "In use", "Subscription needed", "Add answers", the lapsed-subscription paragraph — all attached to the row/profile they describe); QuestionnaireBrowseView.swift + QuestionnaireBrowseViewModel.swift (lines 22-91: "No questionnaires here yet", "Try again", importanceText "Not rated yet"/percentage, authorText "Author not shown"/"Author not named"/name — each self-explanatory in place); QuestionnaireDetailView.swift + QuestionnaireDetailViewModel.swift (lines 19-146, 46-79: counts row labels "Respondents"/"Completed"/"Importance", "How this importance was worked out" info button, "readersSeeText" -> "Readers see: your name" etc., "How this was worked out" sheet, "Nobody has rated these questions yet..."); SubscriptionsView.swift (lines 14-95: "You are not following anything yet", muteText, "Unfollow" swipe action, and the bell/bell.slash icon-only mute toggle, which carries accessibilityLabel "Mute"/"Unmute" and is a widely-recognized mute icon convention, judged close enough to the rule's "universally understood system affordance" exception). AuthorVisibilityPickerViewModel.swift confirmation copy (lines 63-81) and AuthorVisibility.swift displayName/descriptionForUser (lines 26-49 of /Users/scottlydon/Developer/AkinFrontBackModels/Sources/FrontBackModels/Expansion/AuthorVisibility.swift) name exactly what becomes visible and to whom. FollowNotifications.swift explanation strings (lines 60-69) are complete sentences naming who and what. MatchmakingProfile.swift has no rendered UI copy, only a doc-comment example (line 28). interstice/web/panel.html: tab bar ("Cards"/"Book"/"Queue"/"To-do", lines 495-498), companions row ("Recheck", "Dismiss" with aria-label "Dismiss until the next gap", lines 516-517), flashcard actions ("Show answer", "Again/Hard/Good/Easy" with keyboard-number hints, lines 540-546, standard spaced-repetition rating scheme shown directly under the revealed answer), reader controls (lines 584-650, 662-691: "Try again", "Discard it and reopen"/"Keep it", "See the real page" with an explanatory title attribute, "Star calendar", "Switch to day view", "Queue your next prompt" label + "Save"), and the sign-in box (lines 1404-1416: "Sign in to Amazon in Chrome" / "Use the session from your own Chrome instead", each followed by an explanatory "why" sentence) and companions FIXES button (lines 1877-1899: "Play" / "Start a full interval" next to the sentence describing what is off). No visible copy on any of the six targets matched the "(Not this time)" failure pattern of an unexplained control. README.md was not user-facing UI copy and had nothing this rule applies to beyond prose (not scanned exhaustively, as it carries no controls). Grep confirmed no literal "Not this time" string exists in any target file.
entries.rule_title: Every visible label, badge, and control states its own purpose

entries.detail: Profile switcher screen: a blocked row shows "No answers yet" next to link-coloured copy "Add answers" (line 71), but the row's only handler (lines 88-89, `guard block == nil, isPaywalled == false, profile.isActive == false else { return }`) returns exactly when the block exists, so the promised next step has no trigger and no screen copy says how to get answers into a profile; the reader cannot answer "what do I do here" or "what happens when I do it". Same screen also never states, in copy, that tapping an eligible row is what activates a profile (only the "In use" tag after the fact) nor that activation re-runs matching (`onNeedsMatchRefresh`). Fix: ProfileSwitcherView.swift:71 - "Add answers" -> "Answer questions in this profile to use it" as a real navigation target into the profile's questionnaire, plus a header sentence on profiles.root: "Tap a profile to match with its answers. Your matches are refreshed when you switch." I checked the other Social screens (browse, detail, importance breakdown sheet, subscriptions, author-visibility confirmation copy) and their four questions are answerable from visible copy; interstice/web/panel.html and README were not the offending surface for this rule.
entries.rule_title: The sequence of the flow is legible from the copy alone

entries.detail: The paywalled profile-switcher banner (lines 25-31, plus its row label "Subscription needed" at line 81) exists to get the reader to subscribe, but it only describes the situation: "You can still rename and delete your profiles, and you keep matching on the one you are using. Creating and switching need a subscription." No imperative names the action, no timing is stated, and the no-branch is unstated. Replacement: "Tap Subscribe to turn creating and switching back on. Do it before you try to switch, or the row stays inert. If you would rather not subscribe, you keep matching on the profile you are using now, and you can still rename or delete any of them." (Two weaker sibling cases with the same shape are SubscriptionsView.swift:21 "You are not following anything yet" and QuestionnaireBrowseView.swift:24 "No questionnaires here yet", empty states that name no action; I checked the other targets too, interstice/web/panel.html carries real imperatives like "Discard it and reopen" and "Press → for the next page", and AuthorVisibility.swift / FollowNotifications.swift / MatchmakingProfile.swift are model files with no user-facing copy.)
entries.rule_title: Every screen states its primary ask as a direct instruction

entries.detail: akin/akin/Flows/Social/QuestionnaireBrowseView.swift:65 - "Text(QuestionnaireBrowseViewModel.importanceText(for: row))" (renders bare e.g. "73%" per QuestionnaireBrowseViewModel.swift:54-57, "Not rated yet" when unrated) -> add a visible label the same value gets one screen later in QuestionnaireDetailViewModel.swift:53-55, e.g. render "Importance 73%" or place a small "Importance" caption above/beside the capsule in BrowseRow (QuestionnaireBrowseView.swift:51-68), so the reader is not shown a bare percentage on the list row with nothing saying what it measures. Everything else read across these targets complied: QuestionnaireDetailView.swift:46-47 pairs count.value with count.label from QuestionnaireDetailViewModel.swift:51-56 ("Respondents"/"Completed"/"Importance"); ImportanceBreakdownSheet.workingText (QuestionnaireDetailView.swift:93-97) writes each number into a full labeling sentence; panel.html:790-792 and :1345-1348 pair every count with a noun; README.md:42-45's percentages sit under an explicit table header (the rule's stated exception); README.md prose numbers (e.g. line 417, 468) are embedded in sentences stating what they measure. AuthorVisibility.swift, FollowNotifications.swift, and MatchmakingProfile.swift are backend model/contract types with no rendered numeric or date copy, so the rule did not apply to their Date/UUID fields.
entries.rule_title: No orphan data: every number, date, and range states what it is for

entries.detail: Ran rg for the UFC-007 vague-word list across the six targets (Social flow Swift files, AuthorVisibility.swift, FollowNotifications.swift, MatchmakingProfile.swift, panel.html, README.md), then read each hit's surrounding lines to separate rendered user-facing copy from doc comments and past-tense error reports. FollowNotifications.swift:64-69 defines `NotificationReason.explanation`, the exact push-notification/UI sentence shared across all three Akin platforms ("Lives in the contract... explaining why they are being told", line 61). For `.questionAddedByFollowedMember` it returns "Someone you follow wrote a new question." (line 68) unconditionally. But the struct below it (FollowNotificationPayload, lines 90-101) carries `authorId: UUID?` specifically so the notification can name the author, and this reason case only fires when the trigger IS a specific member you follow (following a member is by definition following a named person, per lines 6-9 and the `.member(UUID)` case at line 20) so the identity is always knowable to the app at this call site. "Someone" is an unnamed noun standing in for a name the surface already has access to (the followed member's identity, resolvable via authorId/member lookup, "subject to their author visibility" per line 90). Fix: `"<author name> wrote a new question."` when author visibility permits naming (the `.attributed` and `.unattributedAnnounced` cases per AuthorVisibility.swift lines 29-31, 42, 52-55 both name the author to a follower per the FollowNotifications.swift lines 96-100 commentary), falling back to the current generic wording only for the genuine `.silent` case where no notification is sent at all. Other rg hits in scope were doc comments for developers (not rendered), or past-tense factual error reports ("could not be read", "could not open") which are not the deterministic-behavior hedge the rule targets, or genuine real-world uncertainty (panel.html:1615-1616, "this position may have moved since" describes an unknowable physical-book state, not deterministic app behavior) — none of those qualify as offenses under this rule.
entries.rule_title: No vagueness: every claim names the specific thing

entries.detail:
Rule UFC-008 (row read via python3 csv.DictReader on Recurring_goals/User_Facing_Copy/rows.csv): every "it"/"this"/"that" must resolve to something named on the same surface. I read panel.html in full sections (lines 495-670, 885-905, 1740-1760, 2250-2310) and checked each definite pronoun against what precedes it on the same screen. Most resolve fine: "this book" -> h2#book-title shown above (line 582), "Discard it / Keep it" -> "the device registration" named in the immediately preceding sentence (lines 596-597), "Held here until you want it" -> "your next prompt" named in the adjacent label (line 663), "Wakes Anki and waits for it. Its deck list..." -> Anki named at sentence start (line 897), "this is the copy from..." -> the to-do list rendered just above it (line 1751), and self-referential "this" pointing at the current window/page ("Interstice opens this while your agent works", "this page could not...") is acceptable deixis, not an unresolved external referent. One instance does not resolve: line 625, `
Your agent answered. Go back to it.
`, rendered via window.__latency.complete() (JS at lines 2286-2293) when a background agent task finishes. I grepped the whole file for "terminal", "editor", "IDE" (only 4 hits, none naming where the agent runs) and confirmed no view, label, or prior sentence anywhere in panel.html names the place the reader is meant to return to. "It" has no antecedent on this surface, matching the trigger case exactly (a reader has no way to know what "it" is: their terminal, their editor tab, their chat window). I also checked README.md (self-contained "it" = Interstice throughout, no violation) and the three AkinFrontBackModels Swift files plus akin/akin/Flows/Social (13 files): all "it"/"this"/"that" instances there are internal anaphora resolving within the same sentence or to a label/count shown directly above on the same screen (e.g. "How this importance was worked out" resolves to the "Importance" count row built by QuestionnaireDetailViewModel.counts, confirmed by reading QuestionnaireDetailView.swift lines 44-58 against QuestionnaireDetailViewModel.swift lines 48-55), so those are not flagged. Fix line: panel.html:625 - "Your agent answered. Go back to it." -> "Your agent answered. Switch back to check it." is still unresolved; the real fix is to name the place: "Your agent answered in your terminal. Switch back to see it." (or whatever surface Interstice actually returns focus to — the code needs to say which window "it" is, since the panel never names one anywhere else on this screen).
entries.rule_title: Every referent is named and located on first mention

entries.detail:
Rule UFC-009 (one-pass comprehension) read against the six targets. In-app copy in AkinFrontBackModels/.../AuthorVisibility.swift, FollowNotifications.swift, and the Flows/Social view/view-model .swift files (QuestionnaireDetailView, AuthorVisibilityPickerViewModel, ProfileSwitcherView, SubscriptionsView, QuestionnaireBrowseView, etc.) all pass: every rendered sentence is short, single-idea, second-person, and free of unexplained jargon (verified by reading every Text()/label/displayName/descriptionForUser string in those files in rendering order). MatchmakingProfile.swift is N/A: it is a pure data model with no displayName/description property ever shown to a user, only Swift doc comments for developers.

Two real violations, both against a first-time reader with no domain knowledge:

1. interstice/web/panel.html:882 — `say('Cards did not load. The daemon did not answer: start it with interstice start, then press Cards again.')`. This carries two ideas in one sentence (what failed, and a CLI remedy) and uses "the daemon" and the bare CLI incantation "interstice start" without ever having introduced either term on this surface — a first-time viewer of the panel has no way to know "the daemon" refers to the background process, or that a terminal command is even an available fix from inside a floating panel. Same pattern repeats at line 1228 ("The daemon stopped answering... Restart it with interstice start"). Replacement: "Cards did not load because Interstice isn't running in the background. Open a terminal and run `interstice start`, then press Cards again."

2. interstice/README.md:11 — "It notices the gap the instant it opens, waits long enough to be sure it is real, then puts something you already decided you wanted in front of you: flashcards, your book, a place to queue your next prompt." This is 39 words and chains three separate ideas (detects the gap, confirms it's real, then shows an activity) into one sentence — well past the ~25-word threshold and exactly the "two ideas that should be two sentences" flag, in the opening marketing paragraph a first-time reader meets before any of the product's vocabulary has been established. Replacement: "It notices the gap the instant it opens, and waits long enough to be sure it is real. Then it puts something you already decided you wanted in front of you: flashcards, your book, a place to queue your next prompt." (The rest of README.md, beyond the opening marketing section, is dense technical/installation documentation with many other >25-word sentences, e.g. lines ~54, ~86, ~ many more; I did not exhaustively flag those because that section reads as engineering documentation for a person already mid-install rather than "a first-time user with no domain knowledge," which is a judgment call the rule leaves to the auditor — flagging it here so it is visible rather than silently dropped.)

No account of "the session/transcript/diff" was needed for this rule since its subject is product copy, not agent behavior, so GOAL_LOOP_INTERSTICE_HANGS_AND_AKIN_SOCIAL_2026-08-19_NOTES.md was not consulted.
entries.rule_title: One-pass comprehension for a first-time reader

entries.detail: Read every user-facing string in the target set: all 13 files under /Users/scottlydon/Developer/akin/akin/Flows/Social (grepped Text(...) literals and quoted strings in AuthorVisibilityPickerViewModel, ProfileSwitcherView/ViewModel, QuestionnaireBrowseView/ViewModel, QuestionnaireDetailView/ViewModel, SubscriptionsView/ViewModel, SocialDebugRoute, SocialService, AkinAPI, SocialDTOs); fully read AuthorVisibility.swift, FollowNotifications.swift, and MatchmakingProfile.swift in AkinFrontBackModels (their displayName/descriptionForUser/explanation strings are the reader-facing copy); and grepped web/panel.html (2555 lines) and README.md for scheduling/staffing/retry/quota/cadence/queue-order language ('shift', 'quota', 'retries', 'worker', 'staffing', 'cadence', 'polling every', 'every N minutes'). Followed up on every hit for 'queue'/'retry' in panel.html by reading context (lines 494-1996): these refer to the app's own user-visible Anki queue and a 'Try again' button, not internal backend queueing, retry cadence, or staffing disclosed to the reader. No sentence in any target file states internal polling cadence, staffing/who-else-was-asked, queue ordering, retry counts remaining, or backend terminology to an end user. The verbatim 2026-08-17 trigger phrase and its topic (shift staffing, two-week reporting cadence) do not appear anywhere in these targets; that incident belongs to a different screen (Map Mates venue-ask) not present in this target set. No offending copy found, so no fix lines to write.
entries.rule_title: No oversharing of internals in reader-facing copy

entries.detail: Thought flow built by reading the navigation order in code (Browse -> onOpen -> Detail -> breakdown sheet; Subscriptions; Profiles), not from session recordings or user-testing notes, which do not exist under the targets: at Browse the user holds "whose questionnaires are these and which is worth my time" (answered by authorText/importanceText), and on arriving at Detail from a row of ANOTHER member's questionnaire they hold "what is in this and should I answer it". The second line on that screen instead renders readersSeeText, second-person creator copy ("Readers see: your name" / "...your followers are told it was you"), unconditionally: readersSeeText switches only on detail.authorVisibility and never compares detail.creatorId to the viewing member (creatorId exists at SocialDTOs.swift:52), so a browsing reader is answered a question only the author is holding, and is told "your name" about a name that is not theirs; gate the block on creatorId == member, or move it to the author's own questionnaire surface.
entries.rule_title: Every screen answers the question the user is holding at that moment

entries.detail: Ran targeted searches for banner/courtesy-block patterns (Text(""" multiline blocks, "Before you", "Note:", "Tip:", aside/banner comments) across the six targets. Read QuestionnaireDetailView.swift and ImportanceBreakdownSheet in full (lines 1-165): title, readersSee caption, three counts, breakdown button, question list, and the breakdown sheet's explanation paragraph each name a distinct reader-facing fact (attribution, counts, per-question shrinkage math) with no repeated content. Read ProfileSwitcherView.swift in full (lines 1-95): the "lapsedExplanation" block (paywalled state, lines 25-32) states what remains usable while paywalled, distinct from the per-row "Subscription needed" label (line 81) which flags individual inert rows; not a repeat, both support different decisions (whether to bother renaming vs. why this specific row won't activate). Grepped panel.html for banner/note/hint/companions text; read the header/why-open/companions aside block (lines 484-520) and the reading-view latency/arrival/forfeit/hint stack (lines 602-629) plus their surrounding design-rationale comments (lines 243-289). Every one of those blocks is conditionally rendered (companions aside only paints when `needing.length` is non-empty; latency chip, arrival note, and forfeit banner are all `display:none` until their triggering state occurs) and each names a distinct, non-overlapping fact (why the panel opened once, vs. per-gap fix instructions, vs. time-remaining, vs. forfeit cause). No courtesy/decorative block that painted unconditionally alongside dense always-on text was found. Grepped the three FrontBackModels files (AuthorVisibility.swift, FollowNotifications.swift, MatchmakingProfile.swift) for string literals: these are single-line picker labels and push-notification bodies, not blocks on a dense surface, so no dense-surface stacking applies there. Did not exhaustively read README.md or every Social view file line by line; this is a targeted-search pass consistent with the deterministic_tools guidance (space is measurable, judgment is not), and no candidate offending block turned up in the surfaces most likely to carry one (the dense panel.html screens and the two-block-heaviest Social views).
entries.rule_title: Every block earns its space on a dense surface
